text:
I can't confirm that there was no burning, but the evidence points the same way.

NASA FIRMS recorded no thermal detections intersecting ASSET-F04 between 2026-10-04 and 2026-11-03 (count 0). All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day of the period, so the absence of detections isn't a coverage gap.

However, this doesn't rule out fire. Small, short-lived, cool or cloud-obscured fires may not be picked up by thermal detection. The evidence also says nothing about burned area, the cause of any land change, or anything outside this period.

A defensible wording would be: "No satellite thermal detections were recorded on the property in this period." If you need to show that no burning occurred, you'd need other evidence, such as burned-area mapping or imagery.
